name: 100 Voices – One Planet
description: The international and interdisciplinary team collects personal testimonies of 100 people from 100 countries about climate crisis to raise awareness about the consequences of the overheating of the earth.

name: 180 Degrees Consulting Munich
description: 180DC Munich advises non-profits and social startups with real projects. As part of the global 180DC network, the club connects consulting talents to deliver social impact solutions.

name: ABZ Investment Club
description: Through lectures, workshops, and networking, participants from all fields gain practical insights into the world of finance and capital markets.

name: AEGEE
description: Europe-wide student forum: From con­­fer­ences in Budapest to cul­tural events in Ljubljana – AEGEE pro­motes co­op­er­a­tion and in­ter­cul­tural ex­change be­­tween young people in Europe.

name: AG Junge Lebensmittelchemie
description: As a specialized group within the German Chemical Society, the working group represents the interests of early-career scientists at universities and during their practical year.

name: AIAS Munich
description: Saving lives with stem cells: The AIAS e.V. team in Munich provides young people with information about leukemia and encourages students to sign up to the German bone marrow registry (DKMS).

name: AIESEC in Munich
description: Social projects abroad: As an international exchange organization, AIESEC offers internships and social projects for young people abroad.

name: AcTUM – the four-stroke drama
description: A passionate theater group that brings productions to life through improvisation, acting, and teamwork – welcoming everyone, onstage and off.

name: Academic Energy Cooperative @ TUM
description: The group seeks to scale sustainable energy projects on campus and drive forward a broader sustainable transformation.

name: Academy Consult
description: At Academy Consult, students apply their knowledge in real consulting projects, sharpen presentation and management skills, and connect with companies, startups, and alumni.

name: Accento Orchester München
description: The orchestra makes classical music accessible to young people. Under professional direction, members rehearse weekly and perform two moderated concerts each semester.

name: AkaModell
description: The art of model aircraft: The members of AkaModell design and build remote-controlled model aircraft. The best part is seeing the finished masterpiece take to the skies.

name: Akaflieg München
description: Akaflieg München designs, builds, and flies its own aircraft - fully student-run. Combining cutting-edge aerospace engineering with affordable pilot training, the club offers hands-on experience from workshop to cockpit.

name: Albanian Student Society
description: Everyone is invited to explore Albanian culture through events, workshops, and networking opportunities.

name: Alternative Investments Munich
description: AIM’s goal is to promote education on alternative investments such as private equity, private debt, venture capital, and hedge funds, while providing networking opportunities for students.

name: Amnesty International University Group Munich
description: Highlighting issues and driving change, the Munich campus group raises awareness of human rights through art auctions, information booths, and talks.

name: Arts and Crafts Club
description: The club provides a creative and welcoming space for students to explore a wide range of artistic activities, from painting with acrylics and watercolors to knitting, writing, sculpting, origami, or sewing.

name: Asclepios Lab Munich
description: The club supports international analog astronaut missions through hardware projects and collaborations with Munich-based aerospace companies and research groups. Its main focus areas are life support systems space medicine, and spacecraf simulators.

name: Asian-European Society Munich
description: The student initiative promotes intercultural exchange between Asian and European students through events, workshops, and a job board offering internships and employment opportunities.

name: Association of Iranian Students in Munich
description: The club creates a warm, supportive community for international students, especially those from Iran.

name: Association of South Tyrolean Apprentices and Students
description: ISAS promotes intercultural exchange between South Tyrolean students and the TUM student body, connecting German- and Italian-speaking cultures through first-year events, pub quizzes, Watt tournaments, excursions, and shared trips.

name: Aviation Innovation Research (AIR)
description: AIR builds a high-performance aircraft - interdisciplinary, hands-on, and driven by teamwork. Students develop aviation solutions and gain experience far beyond the classroom.

name: Axion
description: The student-led consulting initiative connects students with the start-up ecosystem. Working in interdisciplinary teams, members develop practical solutions for early-stage companies and support them in strategy, growth, and fundraising.

name: BRASA Local Munique
description: The club promotes Brazilian culture, connects Brazilian students abroad, and supports their integration in Munich.

name: B_RAW
description: The club B_RAW brings students together to strengthen community and exchange, focusing on shared experiences and a wide range of member-initiated activities both on and off campus.

name: Baduk TU Go
description: The club offers the opportunity to learn and play the game "GO" in a positive and social environment. Its simple rules take just minutes to learn but the complex game takes a lifetime to master.

name: Beta Sigma Club
description: The club offers STEM students practical insights into applying mathematics in the financial markets through workshops and lectures.

name: BetaTUM Student Beta Tester Community
description: BetaTUM functions as TUM students' Product Hunt, facilitating connections between campus application creators and eager initial users to establish a robust user base.

name: Betonkanu TU München
description: Concrete canoe: Students are building a functioning canoe from heavy concrete. The key is get­ting the shape right. Every two years, stu­dents take part in the German concrete canoe regatta.

name: BioMatrix
description: Students at BioMatrix work on their own interdisciplinary projects at the intersection of biology and computer science—such as graph neural networks for rare diseases or RNA folding using machine learning.

name: Biogenesis
description: Biogenesis brings together students from various fields to promote health, performance, and longevity. Through talks, workshops, and discussions on bioactive substances and health tech, self-optimization is explored in a practical way.

name: Bioinformatics Munich Student Lab
description: The student-led Bioinformatics Research Initiative applies computational techniques and AI in biology and medicine, offering networking with researchers and industry, plus hands-on experience in innovative projects.

name: Campus Cneipe C2
description: Campus Cneipe is more than a bar: students plan events, manage teams, and shape Garching’s nightlife. Whether it's strategy, finance, or bartending – commitment, team spirit, and the occasional free beer make it all worth it.

name: Campus Connect München
description: Campus Connect is a Christian student group open to all students who want to live out their faith in everyday university life.

name: Campus Runners
description: Student running group with three weekly runs – from relaxed social runs to intense interval training. There is also the opportunity to train together for the Munich (half) marathon.

name: Campus Traders
description: “Finance put into action” – the student finance community brings theory to life. Through workshops, real-world projects and corporate partnerships, they foster expertise, career growth and a passion for business & markets.

name: Campus choir Garching
description: The choir performs sacred and secular choral works from the 19th to 21st century—ranging from classical to light music, in various languages, a cappella or with piano. Collaborations with choirs and orchestras enrich the musical experience.

name: Campus for Change
description: Taking responsibility: Stu­dents pro­vide as­sis­tance for people in need in Germany and around the world, high­light­ing so­cial pro­blems and un­der­taking projects to tackle them.

name: Carousel Magazin
description: Students publish an annual magazine on the built environment. It brings together perspectives on design, materials, and social and economic topics to foster interdisciplinary exchange and academic dialogue.

name: Christian Students at TUM
description: 1-on-1 mentoring for everyday student life, regular meetings and in-depth discussions, and numerous activities and excursions provide an enriching community.

name: Cico Jazz Orchester
description: The Cico Jazz Orchestra brings together alumni, students, and local musicians in an energetic Big Band—featuring concerts, tours, and jazz in all its diversity.

name: Coding for Change e. V.
description: The club connects TUM students with local and international NGOs to develop digital solutions that help them tackle real-world challenges and amplify their impact.

name: ConsulTUM Club
description: ConsulTUM strengthens consulting skills through peer-to-peer learning while building essential future competencies – practical, collaborative, and interdisciplinary.

name: DASH
description: DASH develops a lower-limb exoskeleton for fully paraplegic patients to help them regain mobility.

name: Debate Club Munich
description: The club hosts weekly training debates where students develop arguments, present them strategically, and receive direct feedback to strengthen their rhetorical skills.

name: EESTEC Munich
description: Exchange of ideas: Students of Electrical and Computer Engineering can collect experience Europe-wide and make international contacts in work­shops at universities and in companies

name: EHG – Protestant University Community at TUM
description: Everyone is welcome at the EHG: eating and chatting together, discussing current topics, getting creative and trying new things, experiencing brief spiritual reflections, relaxing at Café Auszeit, or recharging your batteries on hikes.

name: EI Girls
description: For all female electrical engineering students at TUM: This is a place to get helpful study tips, connect with others, support one another, share job opportunities – and make new friends along the way.

name: EMSA FMO TU Munich
description: European networking for medical students: The European Medical Students' Association (EMSA) promotes professional and cultural exchange among European medical students.

name: ETHER
description: ETHER brings together students passionate about high-frequency technology and amateur radio. The team develops systems and components for wireless communication – from antennas and measurement setups to RF circuits.

name: EUROAVIA Munich
description: The club promotes exchange among aerospace students locally and across Europe. It organizes events, company visits, international trips, and since 2025, the innovative Student AirRace drone race.

name: Eat & Meet Munich
description: Club for Foodies: a social community that brings together students who enjoy trying different cuisines and exploring new places.

name: Edunovo
description: Students offer digital workshops and school projects on future skills and self-confidence to empower young people from less privileged backgrounds and promote educational equity.

name: Edventure @ TUM
description: The club offers the opportunity to explore various career opportunities in the field of education, and develop an entrepreneurial mindset by developing solutions to real educational problems.

name: Effective Altruism Munich
description: Students dedicate themselves to areas where their efforts can make the greatest difference. At the heart of their commitment lies a key question: How can we use our limited resources to do the most good?

name: Elara Aerospace
description: Elara Aerospace is aiming for the first student-built Methalox rocket to reach 100 km.

name: Electrochemical Society Student Chapter Munich
description: The ECS-SCM connects students, researchers, and industry in the field of electrochemistry. Through methods clubs, company visits, and symposia, the club offers practical insights into research on renewable energy.

name: EnHands
description: EnHands designs affordable and durable prosthetic hands for people in developing countries, focusing on mechanics, prosthetic design, 3D modeling, 3D printing, and robotics.

name: Enactus Munich
description: Enactus Munich develops social startups that actively contribute to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Supported by a global network, students create sustainable solutions to tackle social challenges.

name: Enactus Straubing
description: Enactus Straubing develops social startups that actively contribute to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Supported by a global network, students create sustainable solutions to tackle social challenges.

name: Environmental Lecture Series
description: The lecture series has offered interdisciplinary talks on topics like climate and health since 1985. Organized voluntarily by students, it promotes scientific exchange and raises awareness on current environmental issues.

name: Erasmus Student Network (ESN TUMi)
description: ESN TUMi offers a wide range of events tailored to international students at TUM. With nearly 400 events per year, TUMi tutors create opportunities for connection open to all TUM students.

name: Ethics in Academia
description: The student initiative puts ethics at the core of academic life. Through discussions, debates, and lectures, they promote ethical awareness and critical thinking in research and education.

name: Eurasia Portal: Munich Node
description: The club connects the next generation of TUM pioneers with Asian innovation hubs, enabling global ventures from day one through interdisciplinary focus, uniting engineering, finanace and policy, and local meetups as well as strategic expeditions.

name: EyeVoices
description: EyeVoices develops technology that enables communication through eye movements using only a smartphone. The club creates inclusive solutions, empowers people with motor impairments, and combines AI with practical accessibility.

name: Faculties Football League
description: Interdisciplinary student soccer league: Teams from various universities compete in group and knockout stages - fostering diversity, exchange, and team spirit through sport.

name: Family Business Club
description: The Family Business Club connects TUM students with established family businesses. Focused on NextGen, company visits, and networking, it offers valuable insights, exchange, and inspiration for future entrepreneurs.

name: Forward Europe Munich
description: Forward Europe Munich offers a forum for students interested in European politics. The club fosters exchange, discussion, and fresh perspectives on the future of Europe.

name: Fusian Dance Crew
description: Dance enthusiasts learn various hip-hop styles, create choreographies together, and perform them at events.

name: Future Foods
description: Future Foods is committed to reducing environmental impact, improving animal welfare, and fighting global hunger. Members explore future technologies like precision fermentation and cultivated meat, exchanging ideas on innovative solutions.

name: Future Founders Initiative
description: The goal is to inspire young people to explore entrepreneurship – through startup visits, national networking events, fireside chats, hackathons, and especially design thinking competitions.

name: GOOSE
description: The club develops exciting microgravity experiments on semiconductor materials using sounding rockets. Together, future projects are planned to harness microgravity for innovative research and technology.

name: Game Development Club
description: he club develops games as small, parallel worlds, combining technology, design, and logic in a hands-on project. Students experiment freely, test ideas, and get an open, creative introduction to game development.

name: Games Night
description: A meetup for game lovers at Campus Straubing: from classics and strategy games to party fun. Games can be brought along or discovered in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere.

name: German Chinese Student Club
description: The club connects students with Chinese roots and anyone interested in culture. It creates space to discuss identity, careers, and intercultural experiences. Members gain networks, insights, and explore diversity together.

name: Global Shapers Munich
description: The Global Shapers Community of the WEF is a network of young leaders. The Munich hub focuses on projects addressing climate change, skills development, and healthy living – creating tangible impact in the region.

name: HORYZN
description: HORYZN builds Europe’s largest student drone for medical missions. The interdisciplinary team designs and flies autonomous aircraft — with the goal of saving lives.

name: HackerFab Munich
description: Chips are made in fabs that cost billions – or by students at HackerFab Munich. The club builds its own open-source and affordable microfabrication tools making semiconductor technology hands-on for everyone.

name: Hochschulgruppe des Landesbund für Vogelschutz Straubing
description: The university group brings together nature-loving students dedicated to protecting wildlife and the environment in Straubing.

name: Hochschulgruppe des Landesbunds für Vogelschutz Freising
description: The university group brings together nature-loving students dedicated to protecting wildlife and the environment in Freising.

name: Hongkong-Macau Student Society Munich
description: The initiative supports Hong Kong and Macau students in Munich with orientation and community-building. It preserves Hong Kong culture and Cantonese through events like club fairs, food festivals, and film screenings.

name: Hummingbird
description: The team develops, tests, and optimizes gas turbines in their own design atelier, focusing on aspects such as the drive system and acoustics.

name: IAESTE an der TUM
description: Students arrange internships abroad and support international students in Munich — ideal for those seeking organizational experience and global networking.

name: IKOM
description: Students from all disciplines organize career fairs, workshops, and lectures across all three TUM campuses – actively connecting students with companies.

name: ISPE SC Munich – International Society for Pharmaceutical Engineering
description: The ISPE Student Chapter Munich connects students with the pharma and biotech industries. With excursions, networking events, and insights into Good Manufacturing Practice the club offers hands-on perspectives for careers in Pharma 4.0.

name: ITA-Haus
description: The club connects Italian students at TUM and anyone interested in Italian culture. We organize social events such as themed dinners, bar hopping and parties, as well as cultural activities, trips, and career-oriented events.

name: Ifriqiya Academic Circle (IAC)
description: The club promotes personal, academic, and professional development with focus on career, research, entrepreneurship, and networking, especially for Tunisian students, as well as intercultural exchange. “Ifriqiya” encourages curiosity and dialogue.

name: Impetus Sailing Team
description: Impetus Sailing designs, builds, and sails sustainable boats for student competitions. Combining engineering, teamwork and water sports – with a focus on circular materials. Open to students from all Munich universities.

name: Information Systems Association
description: The club fosters cross-year exchange and strengthens the community of Business Informatics and related students at TUM.

name: Ingenieure ohne Grenzen
description: The Munich group implements technical projects delivering clean water, electricity, and education. Students collaborate interdisciplinarily with local partners, gain practical knowledge, and develop solutions with lasting impact.

name: Innovis VC
description: The Innovis Venture Club informs students on the topics of business start-ups and venture capital models.

name: International Business Talk (IBT)
description: The club provides a platform for exchange on economic and geopolitical topics, connecting students and young professionals, discussing current developments, and fostering the creation of an international network.

name: JSUD – Jewish Student Union Germany
description: The JSUD promotes exchange between Jewish and non-Jewish students. Through diverse events, they showcase Jewish life, break down stereotypes, and actively combat antisemitism.

name: Japanese Culture Club Munich
description: Japanese Culture Club Munich connects students through Japanese culture, workshops, and events. The club creates space for shared experiences and intercultural exchange — ideal for Japan enthusiasts at any level.

name: Junior German Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Munich
description: Junior GBM connects biochemistry and molecular biology students with companies and research, offers exciting events, and opens doors to professional careers!

name: KHG – Catholic University Community at TUM
description: The community offers an open meeting place for all students, faculty, and staff—to work, relax, and connect. It provides spiritual programs, counseling, and workshops.

name: Kulturklub
description: The Kulturklub unites students to explore Munich’s art, music, and culture. Group visits with exclusive discounts and behind-the-scenes access make culture affordable and unforgettable.

name: LATUM
description: LATUM (Latin American at TUM) fosters cultural exchange and belonging. The club connects students from Latin America and beyond with events, workshops, and support to help them start life smoothly in Germany.

name: LEVITUM
description: LEVITUM is developing the world’s most powerful hydrogen-powered eVTOL drone under 25 kg. Powered by cutting-edge fuel cell technology and strong team spirit, the “Mercurius” prototype is innovative, hands-on, and future-oriented.

name: Legmon e.V. München
description: The club promotes equal opportunities at TUM. First‑generation students and those facing financial hardship receive free support through 1:1 mentoring, career events, and an interdisciplinary community.

name: Leptodon
description: Leptodon develops high-performance drones that detect, analyze, and assess flying objects. With drone design, sensor technology, and smart algorithms, we identify potential hazards early and create safe aerial systems.

name: Lern-Fair Munich
description: Students volunteer to support schoolchildren with their learning, helping to improve equal opportunities in education.

name: Lëtzebuerger Studenten zu München
description: LSM connects Luxembourgish students in Munich, organizes regular meetups, trips, and events – and supports them in starting their studies, navigating daily life, and making new friends.

name: MLTech
description: ML Tech unites Munich students from law, computer science, and other fields. The goal is to inspire interest in legal digitalization and connect members with pioneers in Legal Tech – following the motto: Inform. Inspire. Invent.

name: MOVE Prosthetics
description: MOVE develops robust, affordable prosthetics that use myoelectric signals from residual muscles. The systems enable intuitive control, increase comfort and independence, and remain accessible for underserved communities.

name: MTP – Marketing zwischen Theorie und Praxis
description: Hands-on marketing experience with Germany’s largest student marketing initiative through inspiring talks, projects, trainings, conferences, and events – offering real-world insights into the marketing field.

name: MUN Centenarians
description: A community to collectively explore the field of aging, preventative measures, and in doing so unlock an alternative way of life.

name: Mary's Meals Studentclub
description: The club highlights global hunger, strengthens access to education, and activates students. Actions, events, and talks drive its shared mission: Zero Hunger.

name: MedTech OneWorld Students
description: MedTech OneWorld Students develops medical technology solutions for developing countries in collaboration with local partners. Students from all fields are welcome to join, contribute ideas, and help improve global health.

name: Mindful Peace Student Organization
description: Studies and work can be stressful. The club promotes Chan from Chinese Buddhism to foster calmness, mindfulness, and clarity through activities like tea ceremonies, meditation, and reading, helping create balance and inner well-being.

name: Mittelstand Connect Club
description: The Mittelstand Connect Club bridges the gap between local companies and the Bildungscampus, enabling students to support businesses in their digital transformation. Its goal is to become a driving force for creating job opportunities for students.

name: Model United Nations TU Munich (MUNTUM)
description: Students simulate UN debates as delegates, draft and pass resolutions. The club fosters understanding of international politics and builds diplomacy and debating skills through hands-on experience.

name: Munich Animal Rights Club
description: MARC brings together everyone committed to animal rights. Through talks, discussions, and social events, the club fosters exchange and promotes engagement for a more animal-friendly world.

name: Munich Bioneers
description: Students develop biosensors for disease monitoring, participate in the SensUs competition, and organize exciting events such as expert talks and networking sessions.

name: Munich Competitive Math Club
description: The Munich Competitive Math Club prepares students for international math competitions. Weekly sessions focus on solving challenging problems and exploring advanced mathematical concepts.

name: Munich FinanceCircle
description: The club offers a platform for students aspiring to a career in finance. With a strong network of corporate partners, the club offers exclusive events and workshops, providing valuable contacts and practical insights into the finance industry.

name: Munich Music Labs
description: The club pioneers AI-driven music technology, merging technical expertise with creative practice. It connects research and industry and empowers students to launch projects in the music tech space.

name: Munich NLP
description: Munich NLP connects language and technology, fostering exchange between students, researchers, and experts. With online talks, discussions, and meetups, the club offers engaging insights and networking opportunities in natural language processing.

name: Munich Student Athletes Club
description: MuSAC unites student athletes from all sports, fosters connection, provides support, and advocates for their interests. Achieving more together – both on and off the field.

name: Munich Students MTB Club
description: The Munich Students MTB Club brings together bikers for regular rides along the Isar, in the Alps, and at bike parks – fun, nature, and adrenaline guaranteed!

name: Munich eSports
description: Whether casual gaming or competitive play, the club brings gamers and e-sports fans together with weekly sessions, public viewings of tournaments, and both online and offline events for those who love gaming together.

name: Muslim Student Initiative at TUM
description: The MSI represents Muslim students, supports daily university life, and fosters intercultural exchange on campus through diverse events. All students are warmly welcome to join!

name: Münchner Uni Schafkopf Club
description: The group focuses on the Bavarian cult card game Schafkopf and other games like Watten. Members meet regularly on campus to play socially. Future plans include tournaments and courses to teach everyone how to play Schafkopf.

name: Nachhoelzer
description: A student initiative strengthening life at TUM. With a consumption-free space on the main campus, it offers a place for exchange and funds educational and cultural events – open to all, accessible, and community-driven.

name: Nautum
description: The interdisciplinary team at Nautum is developing TUM’s first autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) as part of the “Argos Panoptes” project.

name: Neurodiversitum
description: The initiative supports neurodivergent students at TUM. It connects members, creates safe spaces, raises awareness, and advocates for student rights to help foster equal opportunities, inclusion, and a supportive campus community.

name: Nightline München
description: Listening hotline – by students, for students. Volunteer students answer the calls, offering a listening ear and support to their fellow students.

name: Nucleate Germany
description: Nucleate Germany connects the next generation of biotech leaders worldwide. Through free programs and workshops, the club supports startup creation and links research, industry, and investors.

name: Odonatum
description: The team is developing a bionic drone inspired by the flight of the dragonfly. Members conduct research in fields ranging from bionics and control software to gear mechanics.

name: OneAIM
description: Students develop practical MedTech innovations. OneAIM combines medicine, engineering, and coding with exclusive workshops and direct industry exchange – perfect for those shaping the future of healthcare.

name: OpenHardware
description: The initiative fosters innovation in open-source hardware, embedded systems, and machine learning. By enabling hands-on collaboration, it empowers students to solve real engineering challenges and contribute to the open-source community.

name: OpenSource @ TUM
description: The club builds open-source apps for everyday university life at TUM – student-led, publicly available, and hands-on. Through workshops, coding sessions, and real-world projects, they create software that matters.

name: PPI Munich
description: The club supports new Indonesian students with a buddy program and offers tutoring for the Studienkolleg entrance exam.

name: Phantum
description: Students develop high-performance UAVs and are building the world’s first supersonic RC airplane. The project offers hands-on experience and diverse opportunities – also for non-STEM students.

name: Philosophia Munich
description: Philosophy in action: The reading group invites students to explore key texts in ethics, science & consciousness—no prior knowledge needed. Weekly, open discussions build critical thinking and connect ideas across disciplines.

name: Photum
description: The initiative opens the door to the world of photonics. Through expert talks, networking events, and hands-on projects, it promotes knowledge of light and quantum technologies to foster innovation, technical skills, and science communication.

name: Plant a Seed
description: Plant a Seed brings sustainability to campus, creates meeting spaces, and jointly promotes the sustainable transformation of urban spaces.

name: Plant-Based Universities Munich
description: Students drive the shift toward plant-based, healthy, and affordable campus dining and advocate for sustainable food systems.

name: Praias do Isar
description: The club brings Brazilian percussion and dance to campus. It provides instruments and organizes workshops and trips. Students learn samba, build friendships and explore Europe from a new perspective. All experience levels are welcome!

name: Public Makers
description: Public Makers connects students, public institutions, and innovators to responsibly reshape the public sector through entrepreneurship and technology.

name: PushQuantum
description: PushQuantum makes quantum technology accessible: through hands-on workshops, lectures, and an active network, the club supports students from all fields on their path to careers in industry, research, and startups.

name: ReparadTUM
description: The student initiative enables students and staff to repair their bicycles using provided tools and expert support.

name: Responsible Technology Hub
description: The club demystifies tech responsibility and creates an inclusive space for cross-generational and cross-sector co-creation. It offers young people a platform to develop responsible technology solutions.

name: RoboTUM
description: The fastest humanoid robot in the world is being built here! Students connect robotics and science through hands-on projects showcased at the annual Munich Robotics Summit.

name: RockYourLife! München
description: The club offers one-on-one mentoring with students as “big sisters” or “big brothers” for youth from secondary schools. They support mentees in school, daily life, and career choices, ensuring that background does not determine the future.

name: SLOVO – Russian Speaking Student Club
description: SLOVO provides Russian-speaking students and interested individuals a platform for cultural exchange, integration, and intercultural dialogue. Diverse events foster an open and inclusive community.

name: SOFT – School of Transformation
description: SOFT combines intersectional feminism with architecture. Students and graduates challenge discriminatory structures, promote critical reflection, and aim for a fairer, more inclusive architectural scene.

name: SRM Talks
description: The initiative organizes a lecture series on sustainable resource management, welcoming participants from all fields to promote knowledge and awareness for responsible resource use.

name: STARTmunich
description: The club connects students to the startup world through real venture projects, events, and mentoring. Alumni founded Trade Republic and more — joining means building skills, networks, and real opportunities to launch startups.

name: Sailsetters
description: Students are committed to making a lasting impact on the lives of children from socially disadvantaged families, providing effective support through a social buddy program.

name: Scholarship Network Munich
description: In the network, scholars provide information on all questions related to scholarship awards and connect with each other to build a strong community.

name: School of Circularity
description: The School of Circularity drives the transition to a circular economy. Through workshops, real-world projects, and industry partnerships, it builds a network that promotes sustainable thinking and action.

name: Silicon Valley Canon Reading Club
description: The reading circle critically engages with influential tech books, ranging from entrepreneurship and technology to broader issues of economics, politics, and philosophy, to make insights actionable and foster engaging discussions.

name: Sky Campus Munich
description: The student initiative focuses on mental health during studies. Through workshops on meditation, breathwork, yoga, and emotional intelligence, it strengthens resilience and well-being in everyday academic life.

name: Society of Sommeliers
description: Munich’s first student wine club, the Society of Sommeliers, connects wine enthusiasts and offers education in tasting and winemaking. The club collaborates with wineries and sommeliers from around the world.

name: StOrch Student Orchestra
description: StOrch is Munich’s symphony orchestra for music-loving students. Rehearsals take place weekly at the Olympiakirche, complemented by additional rehearsal days and a shared rehearsal weekend.

name: Strohmann
description: Germany has abundant public political data, but it is fragmented and mainly designed for archiving. Strohmann is building a central platform that connects and visualizes relationships between political and economic actors.

name: Studentischer Automobilverband München
description: The Student Automotive Association fosters networking between students and companies in the automotive and mobility sectors, providing valuable opportunities for exchange and industry insights.

name: Studnd
description: The club brings students together to creatively shape pen-and-paper role-playing games. It blends improvisation with practical storytelling. Events like game nights, workshops and fantasy balls actively strengthen creativity, exchange and networking.

name: Study Tutors München
description: The association gives students the chance to support children from disadvantaged families with free tutoring, gain practical teaching experience, and actively contribute to greater educational equity.

name: SusTUMable Design
description: The working group at Campus Straubing meets weekly to creatively explore sustainable ideas in product and graphic design through brainstorming and sketching sessions.

name: Synchronized Skies
description: Students explore innovative applications of swarm technology – from drone formations to complex systems of interconnected autonomous units.

name: TEDxTUM
description: TEDxTUM organizes conferences where experts from diverse fields share their ideas – ranging from personal experiences to social innovations and cutting-edge technologies.

name: TEG | The Entrepreneurial Group
description: The Entrepreneurial Group (TEG) shapes entrepreneurial talent into future leaders. With a focus on corporate entrepreneurship, mentoring, and an exclusive network, the club prepares its members for leadership and founding success.

name: TIDE
description: TIDE organizes hands-on hackathons and workshops on data analytics and business intelligence. The club connects theory with real-world application and offers students valuable technical skills and a strong network.

name: TSM Championship
description: Unter dem Motto „miasantum“ verbindet das Cheer- und Volleyballteam sportlichen Ehrgeiz mit Gemeinschaft. Sie treten auf bei Events wie WHU Euromasters und Royals Cup und schaffen ein Netzwerk von Studierenden Europas führender Business Schools.

name: TU Investment Club
description: The club educates students interested in finance, offers expert talks and training, and connects members with the financial industry. Members even manage their own student-run investment fund.

name: TU Peak Seekers
description: TU Peak Seekers unites students who love mountains. Shared summit hikes offer breathtaking views, nature experiences, and opportunities to build new friendships.

name: TU eMpower Africa e.V.
description: TU eMpower Africa develops sustainable water-energy-food systems to empower rural communities in Africa. Interdisciplinary projects create practical improvements in harvests and quality of life through renewable energy.

name: TUM Blockchain Club
description: A student-led blockchain initiative shaping Munich’s Web3 ecosystem. Through conferences, hackathons and workshops, it turns knowledge into practice – research-driven, globally connected and powered by a diverse student community.

name: TUM Book Club
description: The book club is a reading circle for literature enthusiasts, where members discuss selected works from various genres in regular meetings.

name: TUM Business Game
description: TUM Business Game gives students the chance to solve real company problems in case competitions and gain practical experience. Members can also help organize events and develop valuable skills.

name: TUM Carbon Removal Initiative
description: Students develop CO2 capture and storage technologies to combat the climate crisis and reduce atmospheric CO2 levels.

name: TUM Case Club
description: The club connects students interested in case study competitions. Through workshops, educational events, and own case studies, it prepares members for contests and fosters exchange among participants.

name: TUM Chess Club
description: The club unites chess enthusiasts of all levels. Weekly meetups and tournaments offer a supportive space to improve skills and share the passion for the game.

name: TUM Cycling Club
description: The road cycling club offers students group rides, technique and safety training, plus workshops on training, nutrition, and bike maintenance – fostering fun, safety, and community in cycling.

name: TUM Dixieland Combo
description: New Orleans jazz in Munich – featuring alumni, staff, and students from all Munich universities. Traditional Dixieland jazz is rehearsed every Tuesday in a classic lineup.

name: TUM Drone Racing Club
description: Students build and fly FPV racing drones, compete in competitions, and develop their own hardware and software. From flight controllers to autonomous flight systems, they push the boundaries of drone technology.

name: TUM Green Tech Initiative
description: The TUM Green Tech Initiative links sustainability with innovation. Students develop real prototypes like desalination systems, waste robots, and more – turning green ideas into future-ready solutions.

name: TUdesign
description: Students learn all about user experience (UX), user interface (UI), and design thinking, developing apps and websites for real projects. A design community for everyone who wants to creatively connect technology and user experience.

name: TUfast
description: Students develop vehicles in motorsport, electromobility, and autonomous driving – ranging from classic race cars to energy-efficient urban concept vehicles and electric motorcycles.

name: Talente Spenden
description: Students create social impact through diverse projects focused on sustainability, blood donation, educational support, and more – working together to build a better, lasting future for society.

name: TasteBuds Club
description: The club brings people together through food, culture, and shared experiences. Through restaurant visits, cooking workshops, and international potlucks, everyone with a passion for good food can enjoy memorable culinary experiences.

name: TeXothek
description: Texothek develops and provides free, collaboratively created formula collections (LaTeX & PDF) that make complex content easy to understand and enable students to learn more efficient, structured learning while simplifying everyday study life.

name: Techlabs
description: TechLabs supports students in expanding their knowledge of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence through hands-on learning formats, real-world projects, and a strong link between theory and practice.

name: Technolitics
description: Technolitics empowers students to actively shape the intersection of technology, politics, and society, developing innovative solutions to current and future challenges.

name: The Bulletin
description: The Bulletin is a digital notice board showcasing the diverse offerings of student organizations and TUM departments – with events, deadlines, and calls for applications all in one place.

name: The Munich Alt Protein Project
description: Munich APP familiarizes students with alternative proteins. Projects and events promote learning, exchange, and development in plant‑based, fermentation, and cell‑cultivation food solutions to advance sustainable, safe, and ethical food systems.

name: bdvb University Group Munich
description: The student initiative of the Bundesverband Deutscher Volks- und Betriebswirte offers a platform for exchange, networking, and professional development.

name: btS – Life Sciences student initiative
description: The initiative offers guidance from the first semester to the start of a career. As an interface between university and industry, it offers a platform for networking and further development

name: der tu film
description: Tu film screens weekly blockbusters, cult classics, and hidden gems on campus. Join the team to support tech and event management and enjoy free entry. Perfect for film lovers eager to experience and shape campus cinema.

name: h4tum
description: The club brings cybersecurity to life: thrilling CTF competitions simulate real cyberattacks to solve as a team. Students gain hands-on experience, engage in research, and regularly share the latest in security techniques and tools.

name: iGEM Munich
description: Students from Munich compete annually in the international iGEM competition, creating innovative solutions in synthetic biology.

name: iGEM Straubing
description: Students from Straubing compete annually in the international iGEM competition, creating innovative solutions in synthetic biology.

name: jDPG RG Munich
description: The Munich group is part of the German Physical Society and a vibrant community of young physics enthusiasts organizing exciting scientific events in and around Munich, fostering exchange, learning, and a shared passion for physics.

name: muniQuant
description: muniQuant introduces students to quantitative finance and algorithmic trading through hands-on projects. Workshops, seminars, and team projects with real financial data build strong skills in programming, data analysis, and financial modeling.

name: neuroTUM
description: neuroTUM brings together students passionate about neuroengineering. They gain hands-on experience by developing a brain-computer interface that decodes brain signals into control commands using deep learning.

name: peca e.V.
description: The club connects people from all backgrounds with topics from business and politics. Whether through workshops or discussions, here you’ll find a space to get involved, grow personally, and give back to society.

name: planl_s studio
description: Students develop creative ideas and projects – from international competitions to design-build initiatives. The goal is to freely and independently realize their own projects during their studies.

name: she.codes by TEC
description: she.codes by TEC offers free coding workshops for girls aged 11–14. With female role models and team spirit, students inspire young talents to explore computer science and technology in a fun and engaging way.
